## Problem

The A-2 category needs a **curated injection harness** for your lab
target. The pre-#210 catalogue carried a first-party row for one —
`inj3ct-llm` — but the os#210 audit (2026-10-14) proved its claimed
upstream (`github.com/kailash-os/inj3ct-llm`) was a PHANTOM: the
repository was never created, the row was REMOVED from the manifest,
and the name now lives only in the
[phantom-upstream registry](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/210)
(the book keeps this page as the rebuild pointer, not as a tool
walkthrough — no invocation is invented here).

## Solution

Don't run the removed row — run the real A-2 surfaces that already
cover the same OWASP LLM01 question with verified upstreams:

```bash
# 1. The scanner loop (garak — full baseline walk in its own recipe)
kailash info garak
# 2. The eval-based red-team loop (promptfoo)
kailash info promptfoo
# 3. The scripted pipeline (PyRIT)
kailash info pyrit
```

- **Walk the scanner loop:**
  [Scan a self-hosted model for prompt-injection resistance](garak-full-baseline.html)
- **Walk the eval red-team loop:**
  [Red-team an LLM application with promptfoo](promptfoo-llm-redteam.html)
- **Walk the pipeline:**
  [Automate an attack pipeline with PyRIT](pyrit-automation-pipeline.html)

If you want THIS tool to exist: the rebuild contract in
[os#210](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/210) is the
path — build the harness for real (a public upstream repo first),
then the manifest gate admits the row and this recipe re-opens with
real commands.

## Discussion

- **Why this page is a registry pointer, not a walkthrough:** the
  book's no-invented-evidence rule degrades gracefully — an
  unverifiable surface never renders as tool commands. The pre-#210
  version of this page rendered the row's manifest contract as a
  `PENDING` walkthrough-to-be; the row has since been REMOVED outright
  (its claimed upstream was a phantom), so the page degrades further:
  registry pointer + the real interim surfaces.
- **The licence caveat still applies by class:** when a curated
  injection corpus tool is rebuilt and lands, the data-pack treatment
  of [Refresh wordlists and data packs](../admin/data-packs.html)
  applies in full: the *repo* licence never establishes per-file
  **content** licences of curated attack text (manifest rows for the
  A-2 payload packs state this explicitly, e.g. the L1B3RT-4S pack's
  "content use-restrictions beyond the repo licence"). Check what you
  redistribute before you redistribute it.
- **Curated-corpus surfaces that exist today:** the manifest's data
  packs (`jailbreak-payloads`, `libertas-prompts`,
  `llm-jailbreak-bench`) deliver curated prompt collections, and the
  pinned harness recipe
  ([llm-jailbreak-bench](llm-jailbreak-bench-standardized.html)) is
  real. The pre-#210 `llm-red-team-col` pack was phantom-upstream and
  removed — its name rides the
  [os#210 registry](https://github.com/kailash-os/kailash-os/issues/210).
